regulatory_document.title: Application of the Federal Securities Laws to Certain Types of Crypto Assets and Certain Transactions Involving Crypto Assets
regulatory_document.action: SEC interpretive release with CFTC guidance

source_receipts.independence_assessment: The SEC PDF, SEC landing page and CFTC Federal Register page are access points to the same joint SEC/CFTC instrument, not three independent confirmations.
source_receipts.hash_scope: SHA-256 of this exact 23-word normalized excerpt; not raw PDF bytes, raw HTML or HTTP wire bytes.
source_receipts.normalized_excerpt: Examples of digital commodities include ... and XRP (XRP). A non-security crypto asset can be offered and sold subject to an investment contract.

regulatory_interpretation.classification_basis: The SEC says that, based on the listed assets' characteristics, terms and functions as of the release date, XRP is a digital commodity. The release describes digital commodities as deriving value from the programmatic operation of a functional crypto system and supply/demand dynamics rather than expectation of profits from others' essential managerial efforts.
regulatory_interpretation.non_security_asset_transaction_caveat: The release states that a non-security crypto asset can still be offered and sold subject to an investment contract. The Howey analysis remains relevant to the particular contract, transaction or scheme.
regulatory_interpretation.cftc_scope: The CFTC says certain non-security crypto assets could meet the Commodity Exchange Act commodity definition. The cited passage is general guidance and is not a separate XRP-specific CEA finding.

scenario_relevance.institutional_relevance: The explicit SEC asset-level classification can inform legal diligence for exchange support, custody, collateral, institutional products and derivatives, but each activity remains subject to separate law, authorization and product-specific requirements.
counter_hypotheses: Specific offers and sales can still constitute investment contracts even when the underlying crypto asset itself is not a security.
Future changes in network functionality, control, issuer representations or promises, and transaction facts can change the legal analysis.
The SEC interpretation is not a judicial holding resolving every court or every transaction.
scenario_relevance.disconfirming_evidence: The release preserves the Howey analysis and explicitly says a non-security crypto asset can be offered and sold subject to an investment contract.
scenario_relevance.model_eligibility_reason: This is a legal-regime event/context observation. No timestamped XRP price-response study or out-of-sample incremental predictive lift has been demonstrated.

model_admission.reason: Event-timeline context only; not a directional feature pending point-in-time encoding and leakage-safe out-of-sample evaluation.
